capture_blocker.cause: macOS privacy (TCC) permissions, not an application or implementation defect
evidence: screencapture -x /tmp/shots-probe-full.png -> 'could not create image from display' (exit 1), no file produced
screencapture -x -R 0,0,100,100 -> 'could not create image from rect' (exit 1), no file produced
osascript 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every process' -> execution error -1743, 'Not authorized to send Apple events to System Events'

Retried once against the LIVE app window after the dev build was up: `get position of window 1 of process "site-checker"` -> the same -1743, and `screencapture -x -o` -> the same 'could not create image from display'. So the failure is not about the window being absent.
capture_blocker.not_a_headless_environment: A GUI session exists; the agent's process simply cannot reach it.
capture_blocker.probable_root_cause: The agent runs inside a VS Code tunnel/remote server process, which has no GUI attribution, so it can hold neither the Screen Recording grant that screencapture needs nor the Automation->System Events grant that window positioning and resizing need. Permissions attach to the responsible process, so nothing spawned from here inherits them.
required_to_fix: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording: grant to the terminal/host app that runs the agent
System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation: allow that same host app to control System Events
Both prompts are interactive and require a human at the machine; they cannot be granted from an unattended run.
capture_blocker.retry_policy: Per the skill's constraints, reported rather than retried blindly. screencapture did not produce empty images -- it failed outright, so retrying cannot change the result. Exactly one confirmation attempt was made against the live window, then it was left alone.

views.why: The primary changed surface. FR-006/FR-007 reworded the parse-error arm of store.rs::load. Verified textually this run: it now reads 'sites.json is not valid JSON ({e}). Starting with an empty list; ...' where it previously read 'sites.json could not be read ({e}). ...'. This is the one view where before/after would visibly differ.
views.how_to_reach: Before launching, write text that is not valid JSON (e.g. 'this is not a site list') to sites.json. The store is read once at startup, so this needs its own app launch. Doubles as the empty-state view: the list is empty, so #empty ('No sites yet. Add one below.') shows beneath the banner.

views.why: FR-006's other half. The I/O-error arm still reads 'Could not read sites.json ({e}). Starting empty.' -- FR-006 requires the two messages not share an opening phrase. Verified textually this run: the two arms now open with 'Could not read sites.json' and 'sites.json is not valid JSON' respectively, so they are distinguishable at a glance.
views.how_to_reach: Before launching, write the valid seed then chmod 000 sites.json to force EACCES. Needs its own app launch. Restore with chmod 644 immediately after, before the backup is moved back.
views.note: Lowest priority of the three if a future run needs to economise -- it requires a third app launch and a chmod that must be undone.
